clue.text: Picture the killing-it was very close!

parts.note: a picture taken with a camera is a photo
a finish is the final kill, as in being in at the finish of a hunt

explanation.surface: A gruesome snapshot of a murder that happened only just out of shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it was very close!' is what is said of a race too tight to call by eye, settled by a camera image at the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A race decided by examining a camera image at the line is one where the margin was tiny.

clue.text: Man on record as offering assistance

parts.note: a man is referred to as he
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A man is quoted in the files as volunteering support.
explanation.definitionFit: Help and assistance are synonyms for aid given to someone.

clue.text: Try to get a match

explanation.surface: Attempting to arrange a sporting fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international game, chiefly in cricket, between national sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something is to put it to a trial; a Test is also an international cricket or rugby match.

clue.text: Dallied after losing a lid somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters fall into place in some new order
losing tells us to take the word a out of the word after

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wasted time after mislaying a cover from a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing a' turns AFTER into FTER; 'somehow' then rearranges FTER with LID.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally can mean to toy amorously with someone, which is to play at romance.

clue.text: A bit of pointed metal embedded in one's finger?

explanation.surface: A splinter of sharp metal stuck in someone's fingertip.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spike hammered into wood is one sense; the horny plate set into a fingertip is the other.

clue.text: Particular place is destroyed

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so these letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A certain location has been wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Special and particular both describe something specific or distinct from the ordinary.

clue.text: Make can appear chic!

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
if you can do something you are able

explanation.surface: Advice to style a tin so it looks stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Something chic is stylish and in vogue.

clue.text: Nothing can be played on strings by people of no importance

parts.note: none means not any, nothing

indicators.note: be played suggests the letters of the word for can are toyed with and rearranged

parts.note: a can is a tin
strings and ties are both cords for binding

explanation.surface: A musical claim that no instrument can be played on strings by unimportant people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be played' rearranges TIN (a can) into NTI; 'on' simply places TIES (strings) next.
explanation.definitionFit: Persons of no consequence or significance are called nobodies.

clue.text: Sounds as if they're asking to start the pudding

indicators.note: Sounds as if signals that the answer is heard like the following phrase spoken

parts.note: people asking someone to start say go

explanation.surface: Diners seem to be urging that dessert be served.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain used in a milk dessert, a classic British school pudding.

clue.text: Delicate point is made to be stretched

indicators.note: made here means made into something new, so the letters are reworked into another order

parts.note: taken as written
S, south, is a compass point
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fine tip is crafted so that it can be extended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges DELICATE plus S plus IS into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric made elastic, given stretch, such as a waistband.

clue.text: … so he fitted this on his foot

indicators.note: fitted suggests the two little words are fitted together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Continuing a story: and so the man slipped this on.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots carry on from the previous clue; 'fitted' rearranges SO HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear is worn on the foot, and a single item of it is this.

clue.text: Students bone up on their knowledge for this

definitions.text: Students bone up on their knowledge for this

parts.words: Students bone up on their knowledge for this
parts.note: reads as cramming for an exam, but describes both an academic award won by study and the learning itself

explanation.surface: Students revise hard in pursuit of a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant awarded to a student for academic merit, and also learned erudition.

clue.text: Troubled heir in ancient form of receivership?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious successor in an old style of bankruptcy administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receivership' normally means a firm run by a receiver; here the question mark lets it mean the state of someone receiving a legacy.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something one receives on another's death, so it is playfully a kind of receiving.

clue.text: Sticks around in teeth

indicators.note: around says the sticks word is placed round the little word in

parts.note: walking sticks are canes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rods stuck between someone's teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed eye teeth between incisors and premolars.

clue.text: A very fast bird…

explanation.surface: A speedy bird, introducing the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link to 16-down, which shares the phrase 'very fast'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swift means quick; it is also a fast-flying bird with long scythe-shaped wings.

clue.text: Have a difference of opinion about unnecessary radiation

explanation.surface: Arguing about needless nuclear contamination.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarrel or part company with someone; also radioactive dust left after a nuclear blast.

clue.text: … and very fast ships

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: and speedy vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means nimble and quick; a fleet is also a group of ships under one command.

clue.text: Live, at some point, in a small valley

indicators.note: in says the point letter goes inside the valley word

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
W, west, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: Settling down at some stage in a little dale.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or have your home there.

clue.text: Five in one sort of cooker

indicators.note: in says the numeral goes inside the word one
sort here is a verb, to sort or rearrange, so the combined letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people in one kind of kitchen appliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V inside ONE, giving ONVE, and 'sort of' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed heated compartment for baking or roasting is part of a kitchen range.

clue.text: Delay sounds heavy!

indicators.note: sounds says the answer is heard like a word meaning heavy

parts.note: heaviness is weight

explanation.surface: A complaint that a hold-up feels oppressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold off or linger before acting.

clue.text: Some daft error later

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of silly mistake comes afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsequently, at a following time.

clue.text: Any girl who is upset badly will react in this way

definitions.text: Any girl who is upset badly will react in this way

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of the phrase are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl who is truly distressed responds with temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a badly upset girl reacts crossly, and 'upset' also rearranges ANY GIRL.
explanation.definitionFit: Reacting crossly, in a cross and irritated manner.

clue.text: Anyway, it goes round

indicators.note: anyway hints that the word reads the same whichever way it is read

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A dismissive shrug about something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part or device that spins on an axis.

clue.text: A meal I mentioned had a nutritious ingredient

indicators.note: had says the phrase before it holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A dish someone spoke of contained something wholesome.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for nourishment or food, something that sustains the body.

clue.text: Yeast like fungus from rue-a lot is needed

indicators.note: from indicates the answer is made out of the letters that follow, rearranged

explanation.surface: A fungus that, it seems, can only come from much regret.
explanation.definitionFit: These are yeastlike fungi of a botanical genus that forms chains of cells.

clue.text: Skinhead gets ticket for a buck

parts.note: the head, first letter, of the word skin
a ticket or label is a tag

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth gets a pass for a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skinhead' is read as 'skin's head', the first letter S, not a shaven youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer, also called a hart.

clue.text: Singing with joy

explanation.surface: Joyful vocal performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A glee is an unaccompanied part song for male voices; it also means delight.

clue.text: Drunkard taking can opener comes from North of the border

definitions.text: comes from North of the border

indicators.note: taking means the drunkard word takes in another letter

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drinker

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the word can

explanation.surface: A drinker reaching for a tin opener is from up north.
explanation.walkthrough: North of the border, to a British reader, means Scotland, beyond the English border.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Scotland comes from beyond England's northern frontier.

clue.text: Just water!

explanation.surface: Only water, nothing stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere means only or nothing more than; a mere is also a lake or pond.

clue.text: Did he put up poster depicting accounts of the heart?

parts.note: bills are accounts sent for payment
ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: A question whether someone hung a picture showing romantic stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accounts of the heart' looks like love stories but splits into bills and a slang word for the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pastes advertisements on walls does exactly that job.

clue.text: Old South American in North American state

parts.note: taken as written
CA is the abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: An ancient Peruvian is found living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the pre-Columbian empire of Peru.

clue.text: Script not delivered by hand, although produced from the fingers!

definitions.text: Script not delivered by hand, although produced from the fingers!

parts.words: Script not delivered by hand, although produced from the fingers!
parts.note: plays on writing that is not handwritten yet still comes from the fingers striking keys

explanation.surface: A paradox about writing made by fingers but not by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Text produced on a keyboard machine rather than with a pen.
